q: We first evaluate two representative harnesses, mini-SWE-agent and OpenCode, with ten models from two prominent open-weight model families, Qwen and DeepSeek, on three benchmarks
r: Include: controlled comparison of harnesses and models on the same tasks (not issue repair only), evaluation of existing agents.

q: We introduce WIDESWE to evaluate coding agents on such cross-repository tasks.
r: Include: new benchmark with 60 feature and 60 bug-fix tasks, seven agent configurations compared on the same tasks.

q: We applied it in an observational study of ten experienced developers who used GitHub Copilot on an unfamiliar codebase.
r: Include: main contribution is an evaluation workflow for human-agent interaction on a code-change task (human effort and understanding), not PR mining.

q: We measure the pass rates and exploration behavior of 13 frontier models on 84 human-curated core tasks, with 16 attempts per task.
r: Include: new benchmark with repetitions and paired statistics, so the evaluation method is the contribution despite the Roblox domain.

q: We build this planner into Nerveplane, a local-first system for coding agents, and evaluate it with NP-Bench
r: Include: new benchmark for coordination of parallel coding agents with a three-arm design (decision log: coordination benchmarks are kept).

q: We introduce AgentSWE, a benchmark for agent software engineering spanning three stages of the agent development lifecycle
r: Include: new benchmark where coding agents build and edit software from natural-language requirements, with held-out acceptance.

q: Each later event is run twice with the same task, agent, and tests
r: Include: new paired evaluation design (developer history vs agent history) on multi-event maintenance, controlled comparison of five coding systems.

q: We analyze 600 publicly released coding-agent trajectories spanning two agent scaffolds and two language models.
r: EC6: analysis of existing trajectories from SWE-bench style issue-resolution runs, issue repair is always excluded.

q: a benchmark built on naturalistic, multilingual repository tasks spanning eight language groups
r: Include: new benchmark and trajectory-grounded evaluation method for constraint following, 19 configurations compared on the same tasks.

q: We introduce SWE-Residual, a benchmark for Starting-State Robustness
r: Include: new benchmark and evaluation dimension (starting state), five agents compared under controlled clean vs residual starts.
